reference.title: Cable Kneeling Shoulder External Rotation
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching: tall kneeling side-on to the pulley, elbow at the side)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you rotate up, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s up, short pause, about 2 s down

prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen: very light.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then the smallest plate step; longer pause turned out

cues.text: Kneel tall side-on to the cable with the pulley on your left at elbow height. Hold the D-handle in the right hand, elbow bent 90 degrees and tucked at your side, forearm across the stomach; left hand on the hip.
Breathe out and turn the forearm out like a door on a hinge, the elbow staying against your side.
Forearm turned out as far as the shoulder allows without the elbow leaving the side; shoulder blade down and back.
Let the cable turn the forearm back across the stomach slowly, in about 2 s.
Pause, stay tall on the knees, and repeat; switch sides (turn round) after the set.

mistakes.mistake: Elbow drifting away from the side
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow pinned (a rolled towel between the elbow and the ribs helps).

mistakes.mistake: Twisting the trunk to finish the rotation
mistakes.fix: Keep the hips and shoulders square; stop where the shoulder runs out of rotation.
Squeeze the glutes and stay tall on the knees.

mistakes.mistake: Bending the wrist to move the handle
mistakes.fix: Keep the wrist straight in line with the forearm.

kinematics.norm: Elbow at the side (about 0-20 degrees of abduction); Sung 2023 compared external rotation at different abduction angles and positions
From the forearm across the stomach (some internal rotation) to about 45-60 degrees out (clinical opinion)
Pulley at elbow height on the opposite side, so the cable pulls the forearm across the body and the load is horizontal (clinical opinion)
Slow, about 2 s each way (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Kneeling Shoulder External Rotation, video (movement reference)
Sung, Jung, Wang and Kim 2023, the effects of body positions and abduction angles on shoulder muscle activity patterns during external rotation exercises (Healthcare 11(14):1977)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: use a very light weight; the rotator cuff is a small muscle group.
Put a pad or folded mat under the knees.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Knee discomfort: do it standing or half-kneeling.
Shoulder pinching: shorten the range and put a rolled towel under the elbow.
regressions: Band external rotation with the elbow at the side.
progressions: Slower lowering (3 s) and a 2 s pause turned out.

muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Prime mover (with teres minor): turns the upper arm out against the cable.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Helps the outward rotation and holds the arm in line.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Hold the shoulder blade back so the upper arm can rotate.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk from twisting toward the pulley.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Keeps the hips tall on the knees.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Keeps the hips tall on the knees.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the cable's pull to turn the trunk.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the cable's pull to turn the trunk.

guides.label: Forearm turns out like a door
